steps.text: Preheat an oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a shallow 1 quart baking dish.
Whisk flour, baking powder, white sugar, 2 tablespoons cocoa powder, and salt together in a large bowl. Mix in the milk, oil, and vanilla extract. Stir in nuts. Pour batter into prepared baking dish.
Mix brown sugar and remaining 1/4 cup cocoa powder together; sprinkle over batter in baking dish. Pour the boiling water slowly over the top of the batter and topping.
Bake in the preheated oven for 40 minutes. The top of the cake will be set and the bottom will be soft. Invert hot cake onto a platter to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Glendora's Chocolate Fudge Pudding (Cake)
raw_recipe.description: A layer of moist cake forms over soft pudding as this chocolate dessert bakes. Serve hot with a big scoop of vanilla ice cream.

review.reviewBody: This is a true pudding cake that was popular in the 1980's and 1990's. Its not meant to be turned out onto a platter but it is meant to be sponed out into a dish and topped with ice cream or whipped cream. Its delicious.

I love this recipe. :) I did add a small amount of cubed butter to the top of the batter before baking to add richness (1/8th cup), haven't tried it without. Very simple, no eggs- ingredients are almost always on hand. I almost ate all of it myself! Do not invert, keep in baking pan- so cook it in something pretty to serve. Keeps well in fridge in between sneaky spoonfuls. Family loved it! I am making it again for a school teacher appreciation party.

I only give this recipe 4 stars because it is missing a very key ingredient. Dot the top of the batter with 1/3 cup of butter that you cubed. Add it after the sugar/cocoa mix but before you pour on the water.

This thickens the sauce a little bit (not much but definitely less watery) and it really amps up the flavour making this much richer.

I made these as an afterthought with dinner tonight...instead of baking in a one quart dish, however, I divided the batter between four well greased Pyrex 10ounce dishes...they got RAVE reviews. These tasted better than the chocolate lava cake we ordered at a local restaurant just last weekend! I will be making these again!!! NOTE: Do not invert these...either spoon out of the one quart dish or bake in four separate ramekins and dig in to find the fudge-y bits! Perfect served with vanilla bean ice cream and whipped cream!
I made this dessert with half Hershey's cocoa Special Dark and half Hershey's Cocoa. My husband said this is the best dessert he has ever had. And I bake a lot. This is a keeper.

This was great. Some of the reviews said it only needed a pinch of salt but next time I'm going to add the full amount because I felt like it could use a little more flavor. I added chocolate chips in the batter and then sprinkled some on top after I poured the water.

I'm giving this a four as the taste was good, but man, it was a runny mess. Do not, I repeat, do not invert cake to a platter to serve. I had a placemat underneath thankfully, but the pudding-ness ran all over it. I would make again (great chocolate fix), but I would just dish it out from the pan itself and serve with vanilla ice cream or whipped cream. I kept putting the cake back in the oven thinking it just needed more time to bake, but that wasn't the case. I would rate this five stars if not for the consistency- but it isn't called "Chocolate Fudge PUDDING (Cake)" for nothing. Expect more pudding than cake, and you will be very pleased. :)

This recipe is the one my mother made. I followed suit when I left home and that was 45 years ago. I like dark chocolate so in the cake ingredients I add an extra tbsp. of cocoa. A dessert everyone loves.

This recipe is for "chocolate cake and syrup"; not pudding. It is like others have said, "runny" "delicious" "chocolate fix". Make it in a 9 inch square pan; serve right from the pan, scoop out cake, a scoop if ice cream, then top with the syrup. It is wonderful.

This was delicious! I followed this recipe exactly and it turned out perfect! (With the exception of inverting it on a platter, just spoon it out of the pan you cooked it in!) It's very similar to chocolate lava cake. I will definitely be making this again!
I also added more cocoa to this- about 5 tbs more. Very rich, but if you're trying to hit that sweet spot, this is the dessert for it!

In the 1970s I used to make this and lost the recipe! Anytime I looked for one it involved a cake mix. This is the real deal! So easy to put together. Hardest part is waiting for it to bake! It is delicious with some ice cream to cut the sweetness. You will make this again and again!
fabulous and so easy to make
I'd make it again - good recipe.
I made it as per the recipe (except left in the pan as is, didn't invert it) and it was absolutely delicious. Definitely will make again!
Good flavor but not enough of the sauce according to my husband who was comparing it to the same dessert made by his mom. She made it without a recipe so I cannot compare.
Overall it was okay, but do NOT put a whole teaspoon of salt in. It was very salty.
Does this work With-out Icecream?

This is a favorite recipe from my childhood. It's best served warm from the oven with vanilla ice cream. It is just amazing! It's supposed to be runny - the chocolate sauce is built in!! Pour it on top of the cake and ice cream. The sauce will thicken a little after it cools. I love it!
I loved it... And so did everybody else. I think the name would be better called a chocolate lava cake! Delish :) thanks for sharing!
